author: Bennettriesagain
title: Don’t play this if you’re new
content:
I’ve been playing this game since release. While I have in the past enjoyed it, that’s changed recently. It’s so horrible to play if you are thinking of starting now. Wait a few patches till they either decide to fix their multitudes of issues, or just don’t play.

If you don’t care about endgame content or story, which is about 90% of the game, then I guess you’ll probably be completely content with the current state of the game.

I love the turn based combat system, but the shill and powercreep has gotten out of hand and is borderline unplayable for free-to-play and new accounts. The bosses that were designed to shill the new elation path are still somewhat difficult to beat with an elation team. That shouldn’t happen. There is supposed to be a boss coming out that takes 75% reduced damage from non-elation units apparently. It’s annoying to deal with the constant shill. 

The hit point inflation is also getting out of hand, to the point that bosses are literally double their hit points from when they were last in endgame. They have also introduced a new mechanic called voracity that will basically revive the enemy if you don’t do enough damage. It was introduced because of a current quest plotline, but is not tied to the quest itself. If you are early game, you are still affected by it. This becomes an issue with newer players who may already be struggling with fights, and now those fights are much longer and more difficult. While I like the mechanic in concept, it shouldn’t be affecting the fights across the entire game in my opinion, and it has NO place in endgame content. 

This current Apocalyptic Shadow is possibly the worst one we’ve ever had and I think the voracity mechanic effecting apoc is a large factor in that (along with the horrid HP inflation.) Despite having the teams that the apoc nodes were specifically designed to shill, it was still a hassle to clear. I’m not asking for endgame to be easy— I’d prefer a challenge, but this is getting out of hand. They already have an entire endgame designed around the players who will spend money on getting lots of eidelons. They don’t need to turn Apoc and MoC into Anomaly Arbitration. The new pure fiction isn’t currently out yet, but I’ll bet it’s gonna be just as bad. 

As for the story, it’s been rushed and a bit of a mess. I know some of it was because they had to change things last minute due to reasons outside the game, but they should have pushed back the schedule or something if that was the case because planarcadia is messy. No one gets much character exploration at all even when they get an entire SP and Evanescia was so irrelevant it was almost impressive how little would have to be changed to write her out of the story entirely. It hasn’t been horrible by any means, and in all honestly I liked planarcadia for the most part, but most people I’ve seen talk about it were decidedly not fans of it. 

The character designs have become somewhat repetitive and a third of the planarcadia cast has the same exact color palette. 

The rewards are abysmal. You get enough for maybe 50-60 wishes per patch, but that’s assuming you do every single daily check in, event, weekly DU/CW points, and that you are able to fully clear every endgame. Most people can’t/don’t do all of them. That isn’t enough for a singular 5 star, and it’s not even guaranteed to be the one you want. Again, they give you 50-60 pulls over the span of 6 weeks, during which there are anywhere between 8 and 16 banners during those weeks, and that’s not including the 8 fate stay night collab banners. They do maybe 1 event a patch (which again is usually around SIX WEEKS LONG) and these events can almost always be done in an afternoon and give usually less than a full 10 pull. 

None of this has even mentioned the blatant racism, either. There are so few people of color in this game and the ones that are there are either racist caricatures or are basicially grey. It’s like hoyoverse is allergic to color. Arlan is incredibly grey and his kit names are centered around things like breaking chains…. It’s really odd quite frankly. There’s also a black man with “donut lips” in robins trailer. It’s straight up racist. 

The game in its current state is a mess and the people at hoyoverse don’t care about their playerbase or its opinions so long as they can still milk them for money. 

Fix your game.

author: ShadeWolf007
title: Best Game I’ve ever played
content:
Not going to lie, this game is incredible! Unbelievable graphics, I honestly can’t believe something so good looking runs so well on mobile. Even the Home Screen, with the Express soaring through outer space, is breathtaking. Then there’s the character designs. Every character looks incredible, they all have distinct, believable, persistent personalities, and each has their own voice! Background music is incredible as well—I was particularly impressed with the music playing in the background of boss fights, especially with the Everwinter Hill fight against Cocolia. 
I love how strategy is a must in this game— from figuring out which characters work well together, to figuring out what relics to give them, to figuring out what sequence of moves will secure the victory against tons of different enemy lineups, every move can be calculated. I myself love how many playstyles work well— I myself use a 5-star healer, the Path of Preservation trailblazer, and two damage dealers to create a very tanky team, but other styles focusing on DoT, sheer damage output, or even Follow-Up Attacks have all worked well too!
My only complaint is that there’s no PvP whatsoever—I feel like it’d be really fun to be able to challenge other players to duels and participate in tournaments and things like that. Otherwise, incredible game! Keep up the great work, HoyoVerse!
PS: I love Genshin too, but so far I definitely prefer Honkai.

author: Meilani Marie
title: Power-creep & lost the plot (lore and gameplay): and now Blackface in a character trailer. I’m done
content:
I’m going to start with the most recent issue: and for context I’ve been playing since 1.0 with no breaks longer than a week over the years. 

HSR has previously faced criticisms of a lack of racial diversity and insensitivity. But Hoyoverse has reached a new low with the new Robin: Summeretto character trailer: “Chasing the Wind” at 0:57-0:58 there’s an explicitly minstrel/blackface caricature. 

I’d love to give the benefit of a doubt and assume “that’s not intentional blackface it’s just an unfortunately similar design choice”

But the why, in the previous scene at 0:56, do none of the light-skinned characters from the same organization, designs meant to mimic each other, not have the red-donut lips. The signature design trait of minstrelsy/blackface.

Hoyoverse needs to fix it and apologize, and better yet, hire some black people for their art and social teams that will stop this kind of insensitive, if not straight up harmful, cultural depictions in their content. 

Moving onto gameplay topics: 
Despite its issues, I’ve enjoyed this game since it was released. But the design of gameplay has steadily decreased for a while. 

New Units are not compatible with old ones, and team building is uninteresting, there very limited choice or variation in what kinds of teams can clear content. 

The powercreep is awful and few characters are lucky to be strong enough to last more than a few patches without vertical investment. 

They no longer have been buffing older characters with NovaFlare, helping them compete, even if only as a worse option, and there hasn’t been a four* character in YEARS. 

And worst of all: there are limited f2p options. You are guaranteed one free 5* weapon/light cone a year, and there are very few 4* options. Even less that are good for characters. 

And on top of ALL of this. There have been very few events as of late, and those events haven’t had a free weapon(light cone) in over a year. 

The female character design especially has gotten strangely bland. I like that old characters have gotten new versions, but so many new characters are the same basic trend of hoyo’s general designs (short frilly dress with no or detached sleeves)

And god forbid any woman gets pants. 

Boss HP inflation (and endgame mechanics that exclude previous teams) gets worse every patch and f2p Artifact farming and reroll tools are so insanely limited. 

Overall, I do not recommend this game until some quality of life priorities start showing. 

While I’d also love the design and story to get better, there’s been some standout quests/characters that would save it otherwise. But considering the slew of other issues I have, it’s just another straw.

content: I would like to start off with the pros. It is an easy game to get into and a lot less pressuring than other gacha games I have played. I would say the cons aren’t bad enough to not play, but they do exist and are relevant. As of now (4.1) it has been over a year since the last 4 star has released. This long without one is definitely felt. Having little options for replacing characters in team comps makes team building more strict and harder on low spending players. Some teams can go a long time without being given buffs (in the form of a character or direct buffing) which makes some teams archetypes much worse than others. Overall it’s a good game with room to improve.

author: Leonheartsss
title: An endless movie with rich story
content:
This is most story rich game I’ve played on a mobile and it just never ends. Every story told is full of unique characters each with their own stories to tell. There are always a mix of love, hate, personal vendetta, desires, relatable experiences.

There are tough situations that just feels relatable, there are characters that you didn’t like so much but ended up empathizing for them.

I could go on and on, the point is that this game doesn’t just give you the same old rare, or legendary, or super powerful characters for you to spend money on. Rather it gives you a reason to like these characters because you admire them, love their characteristics, and makes you want to be part of their journey, be with them or become them, so that somehow, you are continuing their story. 

The game makes these characters feel alive, and the aren’t just another number, another ticket win, or another pretty animations to you. The decisions these characters make never feel unrealistic, nor do they feel silly, they are well thought out and we might just make similar ones if were in their shoes. 

On top of that, the side stories often reflects the darkness, the negative, the biases, the unfairness or even the moral judgement we observe in the society. You can hate it, love it or don’t feel anything towards these side story characters, but at the end of the day, it sparks that internal debate might happening in your head and wonder if this is really who we are, or who we rather not wanting to be. 

Great story, the game can improve its lottery system, but the story is what kept me keep playing.

author: sytheofdemise
title: Updated Review: Pretty Good
content:
I’ve now been playing this game for quite a few days now and the story is immaculate. I feel in love with most of the characters, and I enjoy how many jades we get in this game unlike genshin. 

The characters are lovable and it feels like you’re going on an adventure with your friends. It feels personal, and the world building is amazing. The graphics are nice, and playing on mobile is quite a delight. The story is clear and even ties in Honkai impact 3rd. It’s clever and I am obsessed with the dialogue options. Your character can be basic, or funny based on the options you choose. You even get different reactions depending on what you choose. I like how there’s even a secret ending— the game is thought out and the developers actually tried. 

The one thing is say is we do not get enough XP or adventure books and such. You have to grind every quest available just to go to the next level. This can be hard since you have to level up to continue the story. I’d say more books would be helpful in quests so it is slightly easier to level up. I do recognize that they do this so players keep playing, but it is kind of disheartening when your character can’t fight anything because you don’t have enough books to level them up. 

All that aside, I recommend this game to people who played Honkai impact 3rd and to those who like sci-fi games with some fun 4th wall breaking.

author: Alienated Intelligence
title: Like a classic JRPG… with features…
content:
Upon first glance my immediate thought was Xenosaga (PS2).  Just the look and feel of the story, characters, and battle system just reminded me heavily of that series… The sci-fi atmosphere, the turn-based mechanics, the way the layouts are mapped out, how the enemies onscreen will target you…. The only things missing are the mecha-robot suits.

Unlike Genshin Impact, which is an open world game with a very loose story with tons of filler… (gameplay, exploration, puzzle solving being the main focus), this game is going to depend heavily on how the story plays out.  So far, the story seems very promising, but something like this can also be a double edged sword if not careful.  It’s still early, and the game can surprise in unexpected ways.  I haven’t played far enough to see how multiplayer may affect things, but for now it looks like it could be worth sticking with.

Genshin’s influence can definitely be felt in this game as character design and sound effects are clearly used as inspiration.  (Although I think that Pom Pom’s design is my least favorite character as it looks so out of place when matched up with the rest of the cast… maybe there’s more of these types of characters?  Just a nitpick.)

As an avid player of both genshin and this I can say both have their strengths and weaknesses.  The real difficulty will be trying to balance between the two games especially since both are time consuming adventure games that require a lot of time to get good, lol.

Either way, wishing for the best.

content:
Great game. I love turn-based games and this doesn’t disappoint. All these people whining about the gameplay being P2W are wrong; they’re just upset they can’t get the “cool” characters. The characters you get at the beginning can be built to your advantage and are full of personality. I’m doing just fine at level 32 with my original campaign team and one character from the beginner spawn. You need to utilize the abilities of your team and weaknesses of your enemies to your advantage; actually read. The in-game guide is actually quite useful if you don’t understand certain aspects of the game.

I absolutely love the story and how it’s progressing so far, not to mention the interactive side quests. It’s not a quick progression either, so that’s great. It is a big game so just make sure you have enough space on your device before actually download it. Also, love the references from Honkai and Genshin Impact!

author: tidusmyking
title: Awesome game, 8/10
content: HSR has both pros AND cons, but overall a really good game in my opinion. Though some people aren’t fond of the turn-based gameplay, having to pay if you want the eidolons faster, and having to spam the screen to get through quest dialogue (as of when I’m writing this, they’re adding a skip button I’m pretty sure??), this game makes up for it by giving you the higher rates to get five-stars compared to its sister games (Genshin, ZZZ, HI3), pretty interesting storytelling, and well designed characters. Additionally, it’s way easier to acquire Stellar Jades (the pull currency) and just pulls in general due to the simple events and the free pulls you can get every patch! It’s easier to farm materials since there’s an auto mechanic, so you can do other things while letting it run idly in the background! In the end, it’s up to you whether you like it or not, but I hope this helped :D

author: Soubs37484488484
title: Room for improvement in audio speed
content:
Fun gameplay, pretty worlds, but extremely boring story that moves at a snails pace. Except, shame on the IPC for bullying Belobog. That is the only thing that really interested me storywise.

I would feel more interested in the story if dialogue had to the option to move at a faster pace, if I had the action to click ahead once I finish reading what they are saying, or if I could skip all the talking and just read it in a manuscript in a fourth of the time that it takes the actors to read it aloud.  Any time they talk longer than a minute at a time, it really annoys me to have to sit there and wait for them to finish their speech every time. That feeling just ended up getting worse the longer I progress in the game. Even if I knew how long the scene is expected to take to play out, like if there were a timer counting down to the end on display, that would cut down on my anxieties of how long I am going to have to sit through the scene.

author: Ir1descentcloud
title: Fun overall, However flaws in recent game content
content: Hsr is an amazing game, down to its story and gameplay. It is a bit lackluster compared to other turn based games, but still enjoyable. However, the power-creeping is absolutely insane. However now her and most other 1.x characters(expect Jingyuan if you have his proper supports) are unusable even in boss fights(if not in casual mode). And these characters are just not good anymore. Sure, some characters have gotten buffs like Silver wolf (not sure if she has gotten it yet?) but they just still aren’t worth using. I am aware that old characters will never be as good as the shiny and pretty new ones but I would like to atleast be able to play these characters without having to redo a battle a good handful of times to beat it.

author: shaojiechu
title: It’s okay…
content: The game itself isn’t that bad, the character design is something that really caught my attention. the designs are definitely better than Genshin Impact! I really like the attack animation. But however, I have to Admit that I put my expectations a little to high. Starting off, I don’t like how the characters have to take turn when fighting an opponent. The cool downs are also very slow…and you aren’t allow to dodge and move around freely during battles. Pressing buttons is pretty much all you have to do. I am a genshin player myself, so dodging is something I expect everytime when I’m having to fight a boss or whatever. In Honkai StarRail there isn’t a choice to dodge. And you basically just let your opponent hit you…there is also no Co-op options. Which I was pretty upset about. Other than the character designs and animations- I really have nothing to be impressed about. But highly recommend if you like clicking and fighting games. If dodging isn’t your thing..then this game is made for you! 😀

author: misham1shaa
title: absolutely amazing :)
content:
I used to play genshin and eventually started playing hsr because of the lesser storage space, but it was actually a lot better than I expected. For one thing, it’s so much easier to grind for levels and I love how you can trade materials if you don’t have enough to level up a character. It’s also much easier to obtain 5 star characters and the tutorial/walkthrough isn’t confusing.

I think the best part is that the trailblazer can have multiple different personalities, and even the NPC’s are expressive — it gives the game a more thematic feel and lets us interpret how they feel a lot better. Over all, amazing game! 

The only thing I think is up for debate is the characters not being able to jump. I probably would’ve gotten more done if they had that feature later on the game. But the no character switching cooldown is really neat.

author: Desert Boat
title: Good role playing, bad leveling & gacha
content:
As a role playing game, the characters, interactions, and stories are incomparably better than any other gacha game I’ve played. This is the only reason I’m not giving it 1 star.

But the game itself becomes tedious after a while. As you level up, enemies also become stronger, so you actually become comparatively weaker than enemies you already defeated (until you grind out to ascend your gear and other stuff to match your level). This isn’t that noticeable in the beginning, but as you progress the grind gets real. It is really demotivating to see trash mobs you easily defeated before now doing much more damage to your team.

Also, the gacha system is ridiculously bad, much worse than most other gacha games I’ve played. The drop rates are abysmal and there’s no pity system that guarantees a five star character after repeated failures. Unless you spend a ridiculous amount of money, forget about getting the character you want and just play with whatever characters the game gives you.

author: Tea6725
title: Amazing Game!!
content: Love this game. It is turn-based combat, with beautiful worlds and characters, as well as an intriguing storyline. I spend $5 some months, and often play completely free. The banners are fair and comparable to other gatcha games. Main character (I picked female one) is the best out of the other games I tried.

author: Pok3n
title: From most F2P friendly to worst.
content: I should start this by saying I played in 1.0. I am also F2P, now that being said this game used to be EXTREMELY F2P friendly. Fast forward to the current 3.2 and you are pretty much required to pull the new characters. I unfortunately didn’t get The Herta in 3.0 and now I can barely do anything. I DID however get Castorice and her light cone but it doesn’t matter because I lost my 50/50 on Tribbie banner. author: white_Winter_Lily12
title: Accessible PS4?
content:
This is an absolutely great game, it’s very engaging and very well plotted, just like many other games, however, like all free roam games, with amazingly thick storylines…you need storage…now, the worst thing about this, is that not a lot of people can afford a PS5 which Honokai: Star Rail is available on, but the good thing about that, is that the PS5 can play games that were originally on disc or store bought from the PS4. 

I generally wish that bigger games like these were available for ps4, strictly because my phone can’t hold too much storage, and it’s not worth buying the extra storage on your phone, nor do I own a Pc (which costs a lot already). Overall, even if adding Honokai: Star rail to the PS4, people who download it on the PS4 will be more beneficial to all people looking to play with just enough storage, and a lot better quality than mobile. 

It’s both beneficial to the devs and the consumers of the game in many different, but good ways. 

Although PS4 storage may not be the BEST option, it’s great for starters who can’t use their phone. We’ve all been there I’m sure… 

Thank you for reading my review, overall, 5-star game, 100% worth the download for a fun adventure. And I look forward to future consideration and uploads Hoyoverse offers to the public! 

Farewell.

author: KoboldCoat
title: A Well Made One Of Those
content: Summary: A good mobile Turn Based RPG that is definitely still a Gacha game. I don’t care for Gacha games. I personally think they’re extremely predatory, preying on people’s impatience and overwhelming them with so many kinds of currency until they decide spending money is the easier option. I’m also not a fan of the idea that I need to pull a slot machine to unlock characters, the key means of interacting with the game’s systems. That said, this one actually has a good game attached. Star Rail looks gorgeous, sounds great, and the gameplay is simple enough to play in bursts and deep enough for me to want to get good at. It has definitely flashed a thousand notifications at me telling me this character is available or this currency is ready for pick up, but so far the actual act of playing the game has pushed all that aside. Looking forward to the addition of controller support.

author: 1mea
title: Out of them all..
content:
Hello! So I’ve been playing Honkai Star Rail since Luocha’s banner. I can say that I have played Mihoyo’s other games as well and needless to say, HSR is the most forgiving game of them all. The systems are easy to work through, and your progress throughout the game is entirely F2P! You don’t have to pay a dime for story, characters, or anything else. You have the option of course to purchase Stellar Jade top-ups, but other than that you’re set for f2p! This game has beautiful graphics and the setting/story is entertaining. If you are looking for a good Gacha and Semi-Open world game to play, then I recommend HSR! 

Things HSR includes!
1: Lots and lots and LOTS of free pulls for characters as you progress through the story/missions! 
2: Side quests!!!! (Very fun, also can give you free characters like Quingque and Natasha!)
3: Easy to use combat system! It a turn based combat fighting style and is easy to use as long as you know what you’re doing! (They have guides to show you what things do as well if you’re new or an old player!)
4: Frequent updates! The HSR community, and of course Mihoyo, always will inform you about updates and if you check your inbox you can see future notices and updates soon to come or past ones!
5: Overall, a genuinely great game.

Slight issue that I thought was worth mentioning!
1: Once you’ve completed the entire story that they’ve released, there isn’t much to do, unless you haven’t completed all the other side quests and other little knick knacks then you’re kinda stuck..

If you truly are looking for a good gacha & semi-open world game, then I recommend HSR to you!

I hope this review will be helpful to you all! ^^

author: Love it! But some EngVA issues
title: Don’t be driven away by the combat!
content: I’ll be honest and say that when the game first came out and I encountered our first enemies, I was a little put off at the turn based combat, but I wanted to give it a shot and I’m so glad I did. After two(?) years of playing, I’m happy. author: NullFantasy
title: A console game disguised as a mobile game
content:
I fell in love with this game immediately after starting. I’ve played gatcha games in the past, and this certainly has the same rolling mechanics you’d expect, but everything else is starkly different from most others. 

The game looks and feels amazing. The majority of dialogue is voiced, story is interesting, boss fights cinematic. Battle takes a turn based approach with multiple teammates. The game isn’t open world, but the areas are wide enough to feel immersive and worth exploring.

author: rowanns
title: Breathtaking.
content:
I am a huge fan of Honkai Star Rail. The game has only been out for a few days and it already has such a massive amount of players worldwide. 

I absolutely love how the quests work in the game. They are designed so you can put your phone down after one quest and pick it back up to keep playing an hour later. 

The graphics in the game are BREAHTAKING, and so are the cutscenes. You can see the hard work that Hoyoverse put in every inch of the game and in every frame of each cutscene. I love how the game is able to run smoothly even on older phone models. There is also a lot of options to customize the graphics in case your phone is lagging, too. 

The combat system is easy to grasp and has very fun mechanics, and the ultimate moves for the characters are stunning. The angles of the camera make the combat look and feel great. 

The gacha system is pretty fair in this game. If you miss a featured character, you are guaranteed to obtain them on your next 5 star pull. There is also a similar system for the standard characters in your early-game pulls.

Overall, this game is a 9.5/10. I would heavily recommend installing it!

author: Nova.Nova.Nova
title: Remember Seele?
content:
Seele was originally a limited 5 star character and the very first one, playing a huge role in supporting the game’s early success. Yet she was powercrept almost immediately, which already felt disappointing for players who invested heavily in her.

What makes it worse is that despite her significance, HoYoverse eventually moved her into the standard banner. For players who spent time, effort, and money to obtain her as a limited unit, this decision feels like a complete disregard for that investment.

Even after receiving a rework, Seele still struggles to keep up with DPS characters released just a couple of versions ago. The update did little to restore her relevance, which only reinforces the sense that older characters are being left behind.

This pattern raises serious concerns about the game’s direction. Instead of maintaining balance and longevity for existing characters, it feels like the focus is on pushing out new units, sometimes even reusing familiar names, to drive more pulls. Meanwhile, older characters risk being sidelined or devalued entirely. Just look at SilverWolf.

At this point, it is hard to feel confident investing in any character when there is a chance they could be quickly powercrept or eventually relegated to the standard pool. That lack of long term value makes it difficult to support the game financially.

author: Louiv32
title: One of the highest casual turn base combat game with endless hours of story and content
content: First and foremost this is a gacha game which has some unfortunate predatory systems to get as much of your money as possible. That aside the game can also be played “free to play” if you can handle fomo well. It has hours upon hours of free content and it is possible to get many characters free to play. If you like anime and deep lore storytelling you will enjoy this game. Character designs and story plus fun combat mechanics that does get crazy the deeper you get in to the game plus optional end game and events. It is an endless live service game that keeps on giving. And if you are a spender it will reward you with many goodies so at least you’re not just buying but investing in-game for future content. There are many gacha games out there but personally Hoyoverse titles are guaranteed to be quality games in my opinion. Remember that even if you don’t spend the game has a whole lot to offer.
